_comment: NeMo Data Designer recipe template for STRUCTURED DOCUMENT extraction (invoices, contracts, forms, specs). Pattern: rag-retrieval → subcategory sampler → llm-structured (drop:true) → expression (drop:true) → llm-text outputs. Copy, replace <PLACEHOLDERS>, adapt output_format schema and section values to your document type.

columns._comment: rag-retrieval: fetches fresh knowledge chunks from the gateway per row at generation time
columns.name: retrieved_chunks

columns._comment: doc_section sampler: picks which part of the document to focus on for this row. REPLACE the values list with sections relevant to your document type. Uses 'subcategory' to vary by topic — map each topic ID to its relevant sections. Or use 'category' for flat random sampling across all sections.
columns.name: doc_section

columns._comment: extracted_fields: llm-structured extracts typed fields from the retrieved chunk matching your document's structure. REPLACE output_format with the actual JSON schema for your document (e.g., invoice fields: vendor, amount, line_items). drop:true means this column feeds {{extracted_fields}} downstream but is excluded from the final dataset.
columns.name: extracted_fields

output_format._comment: REPLACE this schema with your document's actual fields. Example for a policy document:

title.description: Title or heading of this section

key_values.description: Key facts, values, or requirements from this section

summary.description: One-sentence summary of the section's main point

columns._comment: composed_context: expression column (no LLM, instant) combines extracted_fields + retrieved_chunks into a focused context string. Jinja2 template — adjust to highlight the fields most relevant to your domain. drop:true excludes from final dataset.
columns.name: composed_context

columns._comment: difficulty sampler: adds variation across rows
columns.name: difficulty

columns._comment: system_prompt: uses doc_section and topic_path to anchor the assistant's role. Adapt role description for your domain.
columns.name: system_prompt

columns._comment: user_message: generated from composed_context (which combines extracted structured fields + raw chunks). This produces more specific, grounded questions than generating directly from raw text.
columns.name: user_message
columns.prompt:
Generate one realistic user question for reinforcement fine-tuning based on this structured document content. The question must be specific to the '{{doc_section}}' section, answerable from the provided content, and non-trivial (ask for explanation, application, or analysis rather than simple lookup). Natural for a {{difficulty}} audience.

Document content:
{{composed_context}}

Return only the question.

columns._comment: reference_answer: grounded in the composed context for consistency. Goes to metadata sidecar (not training records) — used for grader writing and offline review.
columns.name: reference_answer

columns._comment: judge_answerable: AspectCritic (paper threshold = 1). Does the composed context contain enough info to answer?
columns.name: judge_answerable

scores.name: answerable
scores.description: Whether the question can be answered from the provided content alone.

options.0: Content does not contain sufficient information to answer the question.
options.1: Content contains sufficient information to answer the question.

columns._comment: judge_groundedness: ResponseGroundedness (paper threshold >= 0.5). Is the answer grounded in the content?
columns.name: judge_groundedness

scores.name: groundedness
scores.description: Whether every claim in the answer is directly supported by the content.

options.0: Not grounded — answer contains claims absent from or contradicted by content.
options.0.5: Partially grounded — most claims supported but some require outside knowledge.
options.1: Fully grounded — every claim is directly supported by content.

columns._comment: judge_specificity: Tele-Specificity (paper threshold = 1). Does the question use domain terms from the content?
columns.name: judge_specificity

scores.name: specificity
scores.description: Whether the question contains domain-specific terms grounded in the content.

options.0: Generic — question uses no domain-specific terms found in the content.
options.1: Specific — question uses domain terminology present in the content.

columns._comment: score_relevancy: ResponseRelevancy proxy (paper threshold > 0.5). Jaccard overlap of part IDs retrieved by question vs answer.
columns.name: score_relevancy
